notes: LayerDriver test fixture: standard JIS 109-key layout, simple mode (--calibrate-simple / --apply-simple). Key order follows the keyboard-layout-editor.com (KLE) 'JP 109' preset: row by row from the top, left to right within each row (main block, then the navigation cluster, then the numpad on the same row). Keycodes are the ones that produce each JIS key's own scancode, so on a JIS keyboard several are named after the US key at the same position: ^ = KC_EQUAL, @ = KC_LBRACKET, [ = KC_RBRACKET, : = KC_QUOTE, ] = KC_BSLASH. Why there is no KC_ZKHK: the Hankaku/Zenkaku key (position 17) IS the key at the US grave/tilde position on every JIS board, and KC_ZKHK resolves to exactly the same scancode 0x29 as KC_GRAVE in this tool (KeycodeTable.cpp). Listing both would require pressing the same physical key twice during calibration, so the key appears only once, as KC_GRAVE, and the fixture has exactly 109 slots (US 104 keys + 5 extra JIS keys: KC_JYEN, KC_RO, KC_MHEN, KC_HENK, KC_KANA). Layer 0 = native pass-through for every key. Layer 1 = mostly transparent, with the same demo as test-keymap-us104.json: position 101 (normally Right Alt) is MO(1) instead of RAlt, the number row 1-0 (positions 18-27) becomes F1-F10 while held, and Q (position 40) becomes Esc while held. See driver/KeymapTool/samples/README.md for the full ordered key list.
